meta.title: Selling a diamond: FAQ | Valutazione Diamanti
meta.description: Timing, documents, certificates, payment and criteria: answers to the most common questions about selling a diamond or jewellery in Milan.

slots.faq-contenuto-010: Who should I contact to sell my diamond ring?
slots.faq-contenuto-012: Contact a specialist diamond buyer. La Diamanteria has been buying directly from private sellers in Milan since 2009. We assess each stone using gemmological criteria and, if it meets our requirements, make our own offer, with no auctions or intermediaries.
slots.faq-contenuto-015: Natural diamonds of one carat or more per stone, with a GIA, HRD or IGI report, or without a report.
slots.faq-contenuto-016: How long does an initial valuation take?
slots.faq-contenuto-018: For a quick answer, message us on WhatsApp or call +39 02 466891. With the online form, a gemmologist reviews your request and contacts you; the final valuation is made after examining the stone at our office.
slots.faq-contenuto-019: How is a diamond's value determined?
slots.faq-contenuto-021: It depends on the 4Cs (carat weight, colour, clarity, cut) and on fluorescence, proportions, treatments and certification. We refer to current market prices in Antwerp, Tel Aviv, New York, Dubai and Mumbai.
slots.faq-contenuto-022: What should I bring to the appointment?
slots.faq-contenuto-024: The jewellery or the stone, a valid identity document (required to complete the purchase) and any certificates, receipts or original boxes.
slots.faq-contenuto-027: If you accept the offer, we pay by traceable bank transfer to the seller.
slots.faq-contenuto-036: Direct buying and valuation of diamonds and jewellery from private sellers. Via Vincenzo Monti 47, Milan.

slots.faq-risposta-02: Yes. The preliminary quotation and the examination at our office are free and without obligation. After our offer you are free not to sell.
slots.faq-domanda-03: Do I have to sell after the valuation?
slots.faq-risposta-03: No. The offer is binding on us, not on you: you can accept it, take time to think or decline it.
slots.faq-domanda-04: How are you different from an auction house or a broker?
slots.faq-risposta-04: An auction house or a broker offers your stone to third parties and passes on the best bid, often with commissions and longer timescales. We are the buyer: the offer comes directly from us and, if you accept it, we pay you.
slots.faq-domanda-06: Do you buy diamonds under one carat?
slots.faq-risposta-06: Not as single stones. Jewellery set with several stones, including small ones, follows a dedicated path in the quotation form.
slots.faq-domanda-07: My diamond has no certificate: can I sell it?
slots.faq-risposta-07: Yes. We examine it at our office with gemmological instruments. A GIA, HRD or IGI report speeds things up and may improve the offer, but it is not required.
slots.faq-domanda-08: Do you buy synthetic diamonds or diamonds with AIG, GRA, GWLAB or ALGT reports?
slots.faq-risposta-08: No. We do not buy laboratory-grown diamonds or stones accompanied by these reports.
slots.faq-domanda-09: Do you buy rubies, sapphires and emeralds?
slots.faq-risposta-09: Yes, we also assess quality coloured gemstones, including stones under two carats.
slots.faq-risposta-10: Selected brands only: Rolex, Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, Cartier, Vacheron Constantin, Richard Mille, Piaget and Jacob & Co.
slots.faq-domanda-11: Can I sell a diamond set in a piece of jewellery?
slots.faq-risposta-11: Yes. We assess the main stone, any secondary stones and the setting. There is no need to dismantle the piece before the appointment.
slots.faq-domanda-13: How much is a one-carat diamond worth?
slots.faq-risposta-13: There is no single price: two one-carat diamonds can be worth very different amounts depending on colour, clarity, cut and certificate. That is why we make an offer only after seeing the stone's details.
slots.faq-domanda-14: Why is the offer lower than the price I paid at the jeweller's?
slots.faq-risposta-14: The retail price includes VAT, trade margins and shop costs. The realisable value is what the professional market recognises for the stone today.
slots.faq-domanda-15: What is the difference between insurance value and realisable value?
slots.faq-risposta-15: Insurance value estimates the cost of buying an equivalent item at retail and is usually the highest figure. Realisable value is what you obtain by selling today to a professional buyer.
slots.faq-domanda-18: Can I sell without coming to Milan?
slots.faq-risposta-18: The first quotation can be done remotely with photos and the certificate. The purchase is completed at our office, Via Vincenzo Monti 47, Milan.
slots.faq-domanda-20: Can I sell an inherited diamond?
slots.faq-risposta-20: Yes. Bring whatever documentation you have. If you need an official valuation for probate or for dividing an estate between heirs, our gemmologists accredited with the Chamber of Commerce can prepare a sworn valuation.
